title: Crew Mask Regulator Hose Rerouting Clear of the Sliding Table Runner
abstract: Reroutes the crew mask supply hose away from the sliding table runner after chafing was found on stowed hoses at scheduled inspection, and introduces a hose with an abrasion sleeve and a revised stowage guide.

sections.reason: Scheduled inspection at the five year interval found abrasion on the outer cover of eleven crew mask hoses across nine aircraft, all on the first officer side and all at the same station, where the stowed hose lies against the sliding table runner. None of the findings had reached the pressure carrier, but the wear rate implies a through-cover finding well before the next inspection on high utilisation aircraft, and the crew mask is an item the flight crew must be able to don in seconds.
sections.description: The supply hose is replaced by a variant of the same length with a woven abrasion sleeve over the section that lies in the stowage, and its route between the regulator manifold and the stowage box is moved forward by ninety millimetres onto a new guide bracket fixed to the existing console side panel attachments. The obsolete manifold at the regulator outlet is replaced at the same time, since it is no longer supported and its outlet angle is what forces the hose against the runner. The stowage box itself and the mask are unchanged, and the pressure test procedure is unaffected.
sections.effects: Mass increase of zero point four kilograms per side. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable at part level because the new hose is longer at the regulator end and the guide bracket is new. The removal and installation tasks change, the flight crew limitation entry for the crew mask is reviewed but not changed in substance, and the inspection interval for hose condition is retained.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00231. Retrofit bulletin is an overnight task with the console side panel removed; the kit contains both hoses, both guide brackets and the manifold.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00231, console side panel drilling unchanged
